title: Dell reports a record quarter powered by AI servers
summary: After the market closed on Tuesday, Dell said its quarterly revenue was a record $54.9 billion, roughly double a year earlier. It booked $60.2 billion of new AI orders and now has $132.3 billion of AI orders waiting to be filled. Dell also raised its full year forecast and approved up to $25 billion to buy back its own shares.
why: Dell buys chips and cooling gear to build AI servers, so its orders are a clue about demand for companies like NVIDIA, AMD and Vertiv. Strong orders suggest customers are still spending heavily on AI, even after a rough week for chip stocks.

title: Inflation report and other data come out before the open
summary: Because of Thanksgiving, several reports are bunched into Wednesday morning at 8:30 a.m. Eastern time. They include the PCE inflation report, durable goods orders and weekly jobless claims.
why: PCE is the inflation number the Federal Reserve watches most. If prices are rising faster than expected, the Fed may keep interest rates high, and that can weigh on stocks, especially fast growing tech companies.

title: AI chip stocks pull the market back down
summary: A day after a huge rally, chip stocks fell. NVIDIA dropped about 6%, AMD almost 9% and Broadcom about 4%. The S&P 500 slipped 0.5% and the Nasdaq fell 1.5%, while the Dow rose about 0.9% thanks to stocks like Amgen and Nike.
why: When a stock jumps a lot in one day, some investors sell to lock in their gains. That is called profit-taking. It shows why one great day does not mean the worries are gone.

title: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed for about $41 billion
summary: French drug maker Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $175 per share in cash. That is about 46% more than Insmed's price before news of talks came out. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027 if regulators and shareholders approve it.
why: Big deals like this show that large drug companies are willing to pay a lot for new medicines. That helped lift many health care stocks on Tuesday, including Eli Lilly and Intuitive Surgical.

title: Short trading week for Thanksgiving
summary: U.S. stock markets are closed on Thursday, November 26, for Thanksgiving. On Friday, November 27, they close early at 1 p.m. Eastern time.
why: Fewer people trade around holidays. With fewer buyers and sellers, prices can sometimes jump more than usual on small news.
